This is one of the better litmus tests for whether you’re pushing your use of AI enough or not. 

Up until maybe six months ago probably the best you could do with AI was pull off something you already would produce, but just doing it a little faster. But now we’re entering a point where the output of working with AI can and should dramatically exceed what you would been able to do before, in a fraction of the time.

The product prototype should not only be fully functional and interactive, but it should probably have meaningfully better features than it would have had before. The engineering architecture should be able to deliver performance gains that you wouldn’t have been able to go after otherwise. 

The research for a project should consume every single fact on the subject across every dimension of analysis possible. The business process you implement with AI should operate entirely differently and learn from all its past failures in a way no human could. 

We’re unquestionably entering a period where AI will be smarter than us on most axes. Perhaps not on every dimension that matters (intelligence is still very jagged), but at least on enough dimensions that when we combine it with what we’re good at, you get qualitatively different outcomes.

So the simple test is: if you could have done what you’re doing before AI, you’re likely not pushing it enough.

Yann LeCun and Randall Balestriero just Proved the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, and found a better way to achieve it.

The Platonic Representation Hypothesis suggests that AI models trained on different modalities, like images and text, eventually learn similar representations of the world. But this paper shows that how models are trained matters more than simply scaling them up.

So they mathematically show that, under certain conditions, two JEPAs trained completely separately can learn essentially the same underlying representation of the world. One learns from different images of the same scene, while the other learns from different descriptions of that scene, without ever being trained on image-text pairs.

Their approach achieves the same image-text alignment with 42x fewer training samples than next-token prediction. A 109M-parameter text JEPA even outperforms LLMs up to 72B parameters on cross-modal alignment benchmarks.

https://t.co/3j1enq9qF7

"Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures"

Hybrid models combine recurrent layers with full attention, but this paper finds that recurrent layers learn retrieval faster, preventing attention layers from learning the same capability effectively.

So they proposed Better Layer Division (BLD) which temporarily freezes recurrent layers early in training, forcing attention layers to learn retrieval first before allowing both components to train together.

Across 180M-1B models, BLD consistently improves retrieval performance. At 750M, RULER accuracy increases from 26.53% to 32.82%, while long-context perplexity drops from 12.68 to 8.08.

https://t.co/AuyDXPZk9I

"Training Language Models in Simulation for Psychiatric Intake"

LLMs can answer medical questions, but conducting psychiatric interviews requires asking the right follow-up questions, recognizing safety risks, and communicating effectively with patients.

This Google paper trains an LLM using multi-turn reinforcement learning with simulated psychiatric patients, rewarding accurate diagnosis, effective communication, and clinical safety.

In blinded evaluations involving psychiatrists role-playing patients, the trained model outperforms its baseline in 76.7% of scenarios. Appropriate differential diagnoses improve from 33.3% to 68.3%, while patient-centered communication scores rise from 65.2% to 82.0%.

https://t.co/q4TzUK9OUk

I redid the startup founder signals that lead to top tier VCs investing in the seed / A, after incorporating some feedback.

This added ex-frontier lab and cyber security near the top, IIT as a positive, and educated in China as a negative.

The main changes were;
- extended founding year to 2019-2026, ~2x'd the number of startups
- unified and added some signals

Here are the new signals:

The strongest signal is being a part of a top tier fund before, which seemed odd.

When you look at the examples, this is a combination of GPs, venture partners, EIRs, investors, scouts, scholars / fellowship programs and even interns. 

Seems unambiguous that being close to seeing how the process works and knowing the people empirically is a huge benefit.
